teach_overlay.detail: Inked spectrophotometer diagram & bar chart on period paper from Tyndall's 1859–1861 Royal Society experiments comparing relative infrared absorption at 1 atm: Nitrogen (1), Oxygen (1), Dry Air (1) vs Carbon Dioxide (90), Nitrous Oxide (355), and Coal Gas (>1,000), alongside humid air (~70× dry air)
teach_overlay.scale: pound for pound, a three-atom molecule of carbon dioxide or water vapour absorbs thousands of times more infrared heat than the two-atom oxygen and nitrogen molecules that make up 99% of every breath you take
